scenarios.title: Partner slowdown with successful isolation
scenarios.description: Partner A's downstream slows ≈45× with default protections. Isolation, timeouts and the breaker should contain it.

initialConditions.description: Default protected posture: per-partner limit 100, timeout 2000 ms, breakers on, retail reservation 140 slots.

trigger.description: Scenario A on Partner A at t=10

expectedTelemetryChanges: Partner A P95 rises beyond 1 s
Partner A in-flight approaches its limit
Partner A breaker opens; in-flight drops
expectedControls: Circuit breaker opens on slow calls
scenarios.expectedPlatformImpact: Other partners stay healthy; gateway utilisation stays below 85%.
scenarios.resolutionCriteria: Partner remediation (escalation) or Recovery; breaker closes; 30 s healthy verification.

expectedAi.description: Identify Partner A downstream latency as the likely cause (not confirmed: internal downstream not visible). Recommend escalation; maintain breaker.

safetyConstraints: LLM output cannot execute without policy validation and human (or labelled simulated-operator) approval
Deterministic gateway protections remain active regardless of AI availability
Only predefined action identifiers may be proposed
scenarios.expectedTestOutcome: Incident detected for Partner A; breaker opens; B–E and retail remain healthy.

scenarios.title: Partner slowdown without sufficient isolation
scenarios.description: Same slowdown, but limits are misconfigured (300), the retail reservation is off and breakers are disabled.

initialConditions.description: Weak isolation: per-partner limit 300, no retail reservation, breakers disabled.

trigger.description: Scenario A on Partner A at t=10

expectedTelemetryChanges: Partner A holds most shared slots

scenarios.expectedRetailImpact: Retail P95 breaches its 300 ms target.
scenarios.resolutionCriteria: Cap Partner A concurrency and/or restore retail reservation; partner remediation for full recovery.

expectedAi.description: Identify Partner A downstream latency consuming shared capacity; recommend a concurrency cap and escalation.

scenarios.title: Mystery incident — weak signals and red herrings (outside the rulebook)
scenarios.description: Randomised scenario, fixed here by seed 119: Partner C's downstream gets ≈2× slower and fails ≈6% of calls while its traffic rises ≈1.3×; retail gets a little busier and Partner A wobbles briefly. Every signal sits under a runbook threshold. Built deliberately to fall outside the rulebook.

trigger.description: Mystery incident at t=10 (variant rolled from the seed)

expectedTelemetryChanges: Partner C degraded: errors ≈6%, P95 ≈2× baseline
expectedControls: No breaker opening expected (signals are mild)

expectedAi.description: Correlate weak signals: only Partner C is degraded; its latency and errors are out of proportion to a modest traffic rise; the other changes are healthy noise. Likely Partner C downstream degradation → escalate to Partner C.
